- Streaming pattern: 1) long-lived client TCP stream (SSE/HTTP2), 2) average response chunk size ~600 bytes, 3) typical session length 8–12s.

From Redwood's side we will:

- Share a short mutual action plan and an ops contact for the peering/VPN window.
- Prepare a small on-prem checklist for KV-cache warmup (recommended warmup tokens per model, suggested prefetch cadence).

Attachments: latency-matrix-aurora.xlsx (preliminary budgets)

Proposed short milestones:
1) Aurora runs traceroutes + packet-capture on Tue 1/17 (please confirm time).
2) Redwood runs controlled stream tests from staging to Aurora egress on Wed 1/18.
3) Acceptance run and sign-off by 1/20 if telemetry looks green.

Thanks — I'm looping Priyom and Ben from the infra team for the detailed checklist.

Samantha — quick technical checklist and acceptance criteria from Redwood infra. I'm listing the items Aurora's NetOps should validate; we can walk through these in the packet-capture window.

1) Connectivity and path stability
   - End-to-end TCP handshake should complete within 40ms median when measured from Aurora client to Redwood edge in our us-west-2 staging region; p99 handshake < 120ms.
   - No MTU fragmentation observed for 1500-byte payloads (DF bit set) when sending 1200B chunks — important for gRPC/HTTP2 chunking.

2) Egress corridor checks
   - Traceroutes from the Aust egress IPs (provided) -> record per-hop latency and packet loss. Attach your mtr output.
   - Ensure symmetric forwarding for ephemeral source ports across NAT; asymmetric NAT will increase tail jitter and complicate KV-cache affinity.

3) Streaming/keepalive recommendations
   - Keepalive cadence: we recommend 20s application-level pings for long-lived streams in the presence of NAT.
   - Idle session timeout: any firewall/NAT timeouts below 90s require more aggressive keepalive.

4) Throughput and concurrency budgets (reference numbers)
   - Baseline: 80 concurrent streams per Redwood serving pod (g4dn-equivalent) with p95 token-latency budget of 85–110ms depending on model size.
   - Burst: up to 400 concurrent streams across the cluster for short 30s windows; expect p95 to move ~1.6x under burst unless KV cache warmed.

5) KV-cache warmup & prefetch
   - Recommend a warmup run of ~10k tokens per model per pod prior to acceptance window; prefetch the most frequent prefixes observed in your traffic sample.

6) Measurement guidance (what to capture)
   - PCAP (30s stress window), mtr output, traceroute, host-level metrics (cpu, nic drops), and application logs from both client and server sides.

Attachments included: aurora-egress-traceroutes.png (example tracert), mutual-action-plan-aurora.pdf (MAP with dates). Also updated the latency budget spreadsheet (latency-matrix-aurora.xlsx) with node-level budgets.

If these checks look good, we'll plan Redwood's controlled stream test from staging on Wed 1/18 morning (we'll provide IPs and a small harness).

— Priyom
